summary: South Dakota's sitting senator, Mike Rounds (Republican), ran again and won a third term, defeating independent Brian Bengs. The Democratic nominee withdrew in August.

candidates.name: Mike Rounds
candidates.bio: Mike Rounds has been a U.S. senator from South Dakota since 2015 and was seeking a third term. He previously served as governor of South Dakota.

positions.summary: Describes himself as strongly pro-business and backs lower taxes, a simpler tax code, fewer federal regulations on small businesses and expanded trade.
Says he will advocate for rural health care, VA access for veterans and better Indian Health Services care on reservations.
Supports legal immigration, stronger border security, enforcement of current law and a merit-based system that limits chain migration.
Says education decisions are best made locally and has led legislation to eliminate the U.S. Department of Education.
Supports an "all of the above" energy approach that combines wind, solar and hydropower with other established sources.
Describes himself as pro-life and says he will keep defending the unborn.

candidates.name: Brian Bengs
candidates.bio: Brian Bengs is a U.S. Navy and Air Force veteran and a former Northern State University political science professor. He was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2022 and ran as an independent in 2026.

positions.summary: Says the ultra-rich should pay their fair share, taxes should be lower for small businesses and workers, and the budget should be balanced without cutting programs that help regular people.
Says he wants to overhaul a health care system he calls effectively a monopoly, with a five-stage plan to lower costs and improve access.
Supports immigration reform with strong border security and increased legal immigration.
Says he supports restrictions on abortion after fetal viability, with exceptions to protect the life or health of the mother.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35)
